instruction: On-call: checkout API latency jumped from 50ms to 2s at 02:00 with no deploy. Diagnose.
output:
**Diagnose:**
curl -w 'dns:%{time_namelookup} conn:%{time_connect} tls:%{time_appconnect} ttfb:%{time_starttransfer}\n' -o /dev/null -s https://api/checkout
mtr -rwzbc 50 api.example.com
ss -s
kubectl top pods 2>/dev/null || ps aux --sort=-%cpu | head
**Interpretation:** A sudden latency jump with no deploy often means an infrastructure or dependency change: DNS/TLS degradation, network loss, or a noisy neighbor at 02:00 (backup/scan). The curl breakdown and mtr localize network versus app.
**Fix:** If network loss/latency, reroute or QoS the noisy link; if DNS/TLS, fix the resolver/cert. If the app, scale or fix the dependency. Confirm p95/p99 return to baseline and add an alert.

instruction: Incident: DNS resolution fails company-wide after a router firmware upgrade. Diagnose.
output:
**Diagnose:**
dig example.com @<internal-resolver>
dig @8.8.8.8 example.com
tcpdump -ni eth0 port 53
ping -c2 <internal-resolver>
ip route get <internal-resolver>
**Interpretation:** If external resolvers work but the internal one fails, the router (acting as DNS forwarder/DHCP) broke. tcpdump shows queries leaving but no answers, or no queries at all if DHCP handed a bad resolver.
**Fix:** Point clients/DHCP option 6 at a working resolver (`resolvectl dns` or DHCP config), or roll back the firmware. Verify resolution across a sample of clients.

instruction: Incident: a bad firewall rule locked out all SSH to production at 03:00. Diagnose and recover.
output:
**Diagnose:**
sudo iptables -S
sudo nft list ruleset
sudo ufw status verbose
journalctl -u ssh -n 30
ip route
**Interpretation:** Since SSH is the access path, recovery must use a console/out-of-band or a scheduled rollback. The rule set shows a default DROP or a missing port-22 accept added recently.
**Fix:** From the console: `iptables -I INPUT 1 -p tcp --dport 22 -j ACCEPT` (and established rule), then fix the offending rule. Keep a console fallback and change control for firewall edits. Verify SSH from the admin network.

instruction: Incident: a load balancer health check bug took down all backends. Diagnose.
output:
**Diagnose:**
curl -v http://<backend>/health
sudo tail -f /var/log/nginx/error.log
sudo ipvsadm -Ln 2>/dev/null
for b in b1 b2 b3; do curl -s -o /dev/null -w "$b %{http_code}\n" http://$b/health; done
**Interpretation:** If every backend reports unhealthy simultaneously, either the health endpoint itself has a shared dependency (DB/DNS) or the check config changed. Its failure cascades to a full outage.
**Fix:** Make the health endpoint dependency-light and return 200 when the app can serve, fix the shared dependency, and add a circuit breaker so one endpoint failure does not remove all nodes. Verify nodes return to healthy.

instruction: Incident: an expiring TLS certificate caused a global API outage. Diagnose.
output:
**Diagnose:**
echo | openssl s_client -connect api.example.com:443 2>/dev/null | openssl x509 -noout -dates -issuer
certbot certificates
systemctl list-timers | grep -i cert
curl -v https://api.example.com/
**Interpretation:** openssl shows notAfter in the past; clients reject the handshake. The renewal automation (certbot timer/cron) failed, often due to a challenge or DNS issue.
**Fix:** Renew immediately (`certbot renew --force-renewal`) and reload the server. Fix the automation and add an expiry alert at 30/14/7 days. Verify notAfter is future and clients connect.

instruction: Incident: a data-center uplink flapped, dropping packets intermittently. Diagnose.
output:
**Diagnose:**
mtr -rwzbc 100 <remote-dc>
ping -c 1000 -i 0.01 <remote-dc> | tail
ethtool -S eth0 | grep -i -E 'err|drop|link'
dmesg | grep -i -E 'link|carrier'
**Interpretation:** Intermittent loss and link-down events in dmesg/ethtool point to a flapping physical link (bad optic, cable, or port). mtr shows loss at the peering hop.
**Fix:** Replace the optic/cable, move to a spare port, or engage the carrier. Monitor link state and loss rate. Verify mtr loss drops to zero after the fix.

instruction: Incident: a misconfigured MTU caused random connection hangs after a VPN change. Diagnose.
output:
**Diagnose:**
ping -M do -s 1472 <peer>
ping -M do -s 1400 <peer>
ip link show tun0
tcpdump -ni tun0 'tcp port 443' -c 30
**Interpretation:** After a VPN/firewall change, PMTUD broke (ICMP blocked or MTU too high), so TCP handshakes work but large data stalls. The MTU probe pinpoints the limit.
**Fix:** Lower the tunnel MTU, clamp MSS, and allow ICMP type 3 code 4. Verify large transfers complete and connections no longer hang.

instruction: Incident: a DDoS saturated the network, causing legitimate traffic loss. Diagnose.
output:
**Diagnose:**
sudo tcpdump -ni eth0 -c 200 | awk '{print $3}' | sort | uniq -c | sort -rn | head
ss -s
sar -n DEV 1 5
sudo iptables -L -n -v | grep DROP | head
**Interpretation:** A flood from many source IPs raises device packet rates and fills conntrack, dropping legitimate flows. Top source/distribution and interface counters reveal the attack profile.
**Fix:** Apply rate limiting/scrubbing at the edge, use SYN cookies, enable a DDoS protection service, and blackhole/rate-limit offending ranges. Verify legitimate traffic and latency recover.

instruction: Incident: a stale /etc/hosts entry sent internal traffic to a wrong server. Diagnose.
output:
**Diagnose:**
getent hosts <internal-name>
dig <internal-name>
cat /etc/hosts
curl -v http://<internal-name>/
**Interpretation:** getent returns an IP different from DNS, matching a stale /etc/hosts line, so clients route to the wrong (old) server. Connections fail or hit test data.
**Fix:** Remove/correct the /etc/hosts entry (or the config that injected it) and flush caches. Verify `getent hosts` matches the authoritative DNS answer across affected hosts.

instruction: Incident: a NAT gateway port exhaustion blocked new outbound connections. Diagnose.
output:
**Diagnose:**
sudo conntrack -C
cat /proc/sys/net/netfilter/nf_conntrack_max
dmesg | grep -i conntrack
sudo conntrack -L | wc -l
**Interpretation:** conntrack count near max plus dmesg 'table full' means SNAT ports/conntrack entries are exhausted; new outbound connections fail or hang. Common with many clients behind one public IP.
**Fix:** Add public IPs to the NAT pool, shorten conntrack timeouts, raise nf_conntrack_max, and reduce connection churn with pooling. Verify outbound connections succeed.

instruction: Incident: a proxy cached a 500 error and served it to all users. Diagnose.
output:
**Diagnose:**
curl -sI https://app.example.com/page | grep -i -E 'age|x-cache|cache-control'
curl -sI https://app.example.com/page | grep -i -E 'HTTP|age'
grep -r -i -E 'proxy_cache_valid|proxy_cache' /etc/nginx/ 2>/dev/null
**Interpretation:** The response shows X-Cache: HIT with a stale 500 body, meaning the proxy cached an error response (often via proxy_cache_valid covering 500). Users see the error even though the app recovered.
**Fix:** Restrict caching to 200/301 (not 5xx), set `proxy_cache_valid` appropriately, and purge the cache. Verify a fresh request reaches the app and returns 200.

instruction: Incident: a broadcast storm from a loop took down an office network. Diagnose.
output:
**Diagnose:**
sudo tcpdump -ni eth0 -c 100 -e | head
top -b -n1 | head
sar -n DEV 1 5
show spanning-tree 2>/dev/null || echo 'access switch needed'
**Interpretation:** Rising broadcast/multicast rates and high interface packet counts point to an L2 loop. The CPU/interface load spikes without application traffic. A redundant uplink without STP causes the storm.
**Fix:** Enable STP/BPDU guard, disable the redundant path, and add loop protection on access ports. Verify broadcast rates return to normal and connectivity is restored.

instruction: Incident: after a cloud region failover, some users hit the dead region. Diagnose.
output:
**Diagnose:**
dig +short app.example.com @8.8.8.8
for i in 1 2 3; do dig +short app.example.com @1.1.1.1; done
mtr -rwzbc 20 app.example.com
curl -v --connect-timeout 5 https://app.example.com/
**Interpretation:** Resolvers cache the old regional IPs for the record TTL, so clients keep hitting the failed region. Low TTLs and fast health-check withdrawal limit this.
**Fix:** Lower the GSLB record TTL before failover, ensure health checks withdraw the region quickly, and consider client-side retry/failover. Verify public resolvers return the healthy region.

instruction: Incident: a service deployment caused connection resets because of a mismatch in HTTP/2 settings. Diagnose.
output:
**Diagnose:**
curl -v --http2 https://app.example.com/
curl -v --http1.1 https://app.example.com/
tail -f /var/log/nginx/error.log
openssl s_client -alpn h2 -connect app.example.com:443
**Interpretation:** After a deploy, one tier negotiates HTTP/2 with conflicting flow-control or header limits, causing PROTOCOL_ERROR resets. HTTP/1.1 works, isolating it to h2.
**Fix:** Align HTTP/2 settings across tiers or disable h2 on the affected link, and update the component with the bug. Verify h2 requests succeed and the reset count drops.

instruction: Incident: a disk full on the logging server caused network log loss and false alerts. Diagnose.
output:
**Diagnose:**
df -h
sudo lsof +L1 | head
journalctl -u rsyslog -n 30
sudo ss -lunp | grep 514
**Interpretation:** A full disk stops the log daemon writing, creating gaps that trigger false network alerts. `lsof +L1` may show a deleted logfile held open preventing space reclaim.
**Fix:** Free space (rotate/compress logs, restart the holder of deleted files), fix rotation policies, and add disk-space alerting. Verify logs resume and no gaps remain.

instruction: Incident: a routing change at the ISP blackholed a subnet. Diagnose.
output:
**Diagnose:**
traceroute -n <affected-ip>
mtr -rwzbc 50 <affected-ip>
ping -c5 <affected-ip>
whois <affected-ip> | grep -i route
**Interpretation:** Traceroute ending at a specific ISP hop with no further progress (or an ICMP unreachable) indicates a blackhole. The subnet is advertised but the path drops, often after a route change.
**Fix:** Engage the ISP with traceroute evidence, or advertise the prefix via an alternate path/BGP policy. As a mitigation, shift traffic to a different region/anycast. Verify reachability returns.

instruction: Incident: all pods lost network after a CNI upgrade. Diagnose.
output:
**Diagnose:**
kubectl get pods -A -o wide
kubectl logs -n kube-system <cni-pod> --tail=50
ip link show
sudo tcpdump -ni any host <pod-ip> -c 20
ip route show
**Interpretation:** If pods are Running but unreachable, the CNI failed to program routes/overlays. CNI logs show errors, and the host may lack routes to pod CIDRs.
**Fix:** Roll back the CNI to the previous version, restart the CNI daemonset, and verify pod-to-pod connectivity. Check the overlay MTU too. Confirm with a test pod connection.

instruction: Incident: a time change (NTP) broke TLS with certificate-not-yet-valid errors. Diagnose.
output:
**Diagnose:**
date -u
sudo timedatectl
chronyc tracking 2>/dev/null || ntpq -p
openssl x509 -noout -dates -in cert.pem
**Interpretation:** If the host clock jumped ahead/behind, TLS validation fails with not-yet-valid or expired errors even though the cert is fine. timedatectl shows 'synchronized: no'.
**Fix:** Enable/repoint NTP (`timedatectl set-ntp true`), force a sync (`chronyc makestep`), and correct the timezone only for display. Verify time is accurate and TLS works.

instruction: Incident: an autoscaling stampede caused connection storms and backend overload after a traffic spike. Diagnose.
output:
**Diagnose:**
sudo ss -s
kubectl get hpa -A 2>/dev/null
curl -w 'conn:%{time_connect} ttfb:%{time_starttransfer}\n' -o /dev/null -s https://app/
kubectl get pods -w 2>/dev/null | head
**Interpretation:** Rapid scale-out/failover made many clients reconnect at once, flooding the backend and DNS, which slows everything and can cause flapping. High TIME_WAIT and connection counts confirm.
**Fix:** Add connection pooling/jittered retries, tune autoscaling cooldowns and health checks, and pre-warm capacity. Verify connection storm subsides and latency stabilizes.

instruction: Incident: a cable/optic failure caused BER errors and silent data corruption suspected. Diagnose.
output:
**Diagnose:**
ethtool -S eth0 | grep -i -E 'crc|error|ber|discard'
ethtool eth0
ip -s link show eth0
dmesg | grep -i eth0
**Interpretation:** Rising CRC/FCS/error counters and a link that stays up but corrupts frames indicate a marginal optic/cable. TCP retransmissions mask it as slowness, not full failure.
**Fix:** Replace the optic/cable and test the replacement, monitoring error counters. Verify CRC errors stop and throughput/retransmits normalize.
